=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:150-280 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The new `memory_validation_history_*`, `memory_operator_bypass_audit_*`, and `memory_revalidate_events_*` shell helpers are defined but not exported, so downstream callers that expect exported shell functions cannot invoke them.
  WHY: One reviewer says the repo intentionally uses sourced shell helpers without `export -f`, so the impact is disputed, but the reported behavior would make external consumers unable to call the new wrappers.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:941-1067 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Each append helper normalizes the payload twice, repeating the normalize/sort/validate work on every append.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers report the second normalize/sort pass as redundant; one reviewer argues the pre-append normalize is necessary, so the inefficiency is disputed but still repeatedly reported.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:817-855 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_stable_sort_entries_by_field` is applied during payload normalization on every write, so append operations pay repeated O(N log N) sorting cost as histories grow.
  WHY: The helper preserves equal-timestamp order correctly, but both reviewers who flagged it treated the repeated sort as avoidable overhead.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:618-626 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Malformed ISO datetimes in `_normalize_datetime_utc` are reported inconsistently, with reviewers saying they can surface as raw exceptions instead of a structured `MemoryValidationError`.
  WHY: One reviewer says the helper wraps `ValueError`, but others still reported malformed timestamps escaping the intended fail-open validation path.
- scripts/ai_memory.py:863-874,975-991,1110-1125,1230-1245,1350-1365 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The append commands catch validation, JSON, I/O, `ValueError`, and `MemoryGitError` together and always emit generic fail-open warnings, so callers cannot distinguish the failure class and append-side responses lack the `warning_code` metadata used on get-side fallbacks.
  WHY: This collapses distinct causes into one path and hides whether the failure was bad entry data, corruption, or a git problem.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:981-1363 | severity=low | confidence=4

  WHY: Calling `get_*()` or default creation, then normalizing again after appending the new entry, repeats the same payload work without changing the result.

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:817-855 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The stable-sort helper is applied again on every append even though the per-entry normalizers already produce a correctly ordered list.
  WHY: This adds unnecessary O(N log N) work on every append and duplicates the ordering pass.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:618-626 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A malformed ISO datetime can raise a raw `ValueError` before `MemoryValidationError` is raised, and the caller only sees a coarse append fallback warning.
  WHY: The reviewer reports that callers lose actionable diagnostics because the warning path does not preserve the underlying datetime failure cleanly.
- scripts/ai_memory.py:863-874,975-991,1110-1125,1230-1245,1350-1365 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The append command `except` blocks are too broad and flatten git, validation, JSON, and I/O failures into the same generic warning path.
  WHY: Downstream orchestration cannot reliably distinguish a temporary memory-branch problem from bad entry data without parsing the free-form warning string.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
